summary: The lecture covers Part II of the Indian Constitution (Articles 5–11) on Citizenship, the Citizenship Act 1955, five modes of acquiring citizenship, three modes of losing it, the distinction between nationality and citizenship, single vs dual citizenship, categories of overseas Indians (NRI, PIO, OCI), and the Citizenship Amendment Act 2019 with its key provisions.
points: Part II (Articles 5–11) deals with Citizenship; Citizenship Act 1955 details acquisition/termination.
India has single citizenship; no dual citizenship unlike USA/Switzerland.
Five modes to acquire citizenship: birth, descent, registration, naturalization, incorporation of territory.
Citizenship by birth after 3 Dec 2004: one Indian parent, other not illegal migrant, registration within 1 year.
Citizenship by descent after 3 Dec 2004: birth registered at Indian consulate within 1 year.
Naturalization requires 12 years residence (1 year if govt service), good character, 8th Schedule language.
Citizenship lost by renunciation, termination (auto on foreign citizenship), deprivation (fraud, etc.).
CAA 2019 reduces residency to 6 years for 6 minorities from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Pakistan entering before 31 Dec 2014.
OCI card (merged PIO 2015) gives lifelong visa, no voting rights; excludes 7 neighboring countries.
Nationality is automatic by birth, unchangeable; citizenship is legal status, changeable.

check.q: Which Article empowers Parliament to regulate citizenship?
Under CAA 2019, what is the reduced residency period for eligible migrants?
Which overseas Indian category was merged with OCI in 2015?
